notes:
Product / technical notes (copied from calls, shorthand):
- Company: Spectral IDEworks — building an IDE copilot focused on low-latency line/statement completions and multi-file code actions. Primary customers are developer teams where interruption cost is high.
- Primary ask: 'TTFT as perceived by dev should be near instantaneous' — customer wants median TTFT < 60ms, p95 < 150ms for single-line completions. Jitter budget < 20ms observed at client.
- Use pattern: short completions (8-40 tokens) 75% of calls, occasional multi-line (200-600 tokens) for refactors. Peak concurrency: 400-600 concurrent devs in day-to-day; POC will emulate 500.
- Token budget tuning: want budget per request to be adaptive (base 64 tokens) with continuation prefetch on idle/anticipation heuristics. Concerned about runaway costs when long refactors trigger continuation loops.
- Streaming strategy: prefer sub-token/word streaming to update editor UI progressively; need low TTFT and small first-chunk sizes to avoid perceived lag. Client expects first token within target TTFT and then smooth stream.
- Backpressure & graceful degradation: when overloaded, fallback to 'best-effort single-shot' completion with truncated context rather than queuing long. Also want explicit header to indicate whether streaming is partial/complete for editor UX.
- Model/version pinning: must pin to a code-specialized model; QA requirement: ability to pin stable model and fallback to a quantized cheaper variant when Dedicated capacity constrained. Must support canary rollouts for model upgrades (A/B).
- Cost/perf concerns: aware of batching benefits but worried about batching-induced TTFT increases. Seeking guidance from Redwood Optimize on batching thresholds that don't violate TTFT targets.
- Security/compliance: VPC + SSO (SAML) required, audit logs for every token stream session, ability to set retention controls per customer workspace. KMS for keying.
- Quotes: 'If completions feel slow, devs treat the copilot as a toy' — product lead.
- POC success criteria: median TTFT < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, jitter < 20ms, cost per active dev < $X (to be defined), streaming reliability > 99.5% over 1 week load test.
- Engineering notes: plugin team will add hook for chunked transfer encoding and client-side incremental renderer; need example SDK and a streaming contract (first-chunk latency guarantees + backpressure signals).
- Open items: exact token budget defaults, expected cost per 1k tokens for hosted vs dedicated, SLA language for TTFT in contract.
- Next: deliver POC plan + test harness (load scripts), Redwood to provide sample streaming SDK and recommended kernel/quantization profile.
